paragraphs: Friend, God could have sent Ezekiel a scroll or a trumpet. Instead He gave him a brick, an iron plate, 390 days on one side and bread weighed out by the day. God said all of it would be "a sign to the house of Israel" (Ezekiel 4:3). I think that tells us something: God wanted His people to see the warning, not just hear it.

And the warning was heavy. God says He will "cut off the supply of food in Jerusalem," and that the people will be "appalled at the sight of one another wasting away in their iniquity" (Ezekiel 4:16-17). Ezekiel bore the iniquity of Israel and Judah, day after day, and the sin was real. But look at Ezekiel 4:14-15. Ezekiel speaks up to God, and God answers him and changes what the bread is baked over. God is serious about sin, friend, and He still hears His servant when he speaks.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery. When God warns, He is not being cruel. He is being clear. If He took the trouble to act out a warning in front of the people, then His Word is worth taking seriously, and worth acting on while there is time. Listen to Him, talk to Him, and let Him get you ready, because my ovens stay ready and so should we.
